title: When the Compass Sings
premise: Silas Dravenmoor, a disgraced mountain guide hiding from the fallout of an expedition that went wrong in two countries, takes one last paid job leading a wealthy patron's team to a sea cave revealed only at low tide beneath a calving glacier. Inside, they find evidence that rewrites the region's history—and proof that Silas's old expedition partner, long presumed dead, may have survived. Torn between loyalty to her lost friend and the truth owed to the families still grieving, Silas must lead everyone out before the glacier calves and seals the route forever. In the end she chooses truth over silence, confessing what really happened years ago and losing her anonymity but finally earning a place to belong.
about_author: Edmund Montrose is the pen name of a former expedition cook who spent a decade in base camps across three continents before turning to fiction. He writes adventure stories about people who run from their pasts and the landscapes that refuse to let them.

chapters.title: The Weight of Moving On
chapters.summary: Third-person limited from Silas's POV. Silas works a low-stakes guiding job in a coastal town, keeping her head down and her name off manifests. A letter arrives offering triple pay for a short-notice glacier expedition. She almost burns it; rent and a debt to a smuggler say otherwise. Emotional beat: exhaustion disguised as freedom.

chapters.title: Patrons and Ghosts
chapters.summary: Silas meets the client, Aldous Vane, a collector whose charm barely covers his obsession with the legendary Siren Cave. Among the hired crew is Tomas Reyes—a man who once testified against her. She nearly walks, but Vane's advance clears her debt. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: paranoia sharpening into resolve.

chapters.title: Cold Company
chapters.summary: The team treks toward the glacier. Silas proves her skill reading ice and weather, slowly winning grudging respect—except from Tomas, who needles her about 'the Kernvall incident.' At night she studies tide charts: the cave opens for under six hours, twice, before calving season. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: competence as armor.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: First window: the team enters the cave at extreme low tide. They find carved markers predating any known settlement—and a rusted carabiner stamped with the logo of Silas's doomed Kernvall expedition. She pockets it before anyone sees. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: dread blooming inside wonder.

chapters.title: The Man Who Wasn't Buried
chapters.summary: Deeper chamber: a sheltered alcove with supplies, a journal, and dates continuing past the avalanche that killed her partner Wren Halloway. The handwriting is Wren's. The final entry warns someone else has been coming here. POV alternates Silas and journal excerpts. Emotional beat: grief cracking open into hope.

chapters.title: Vane's Bargain
chapters.summary: Aldous discovers the artifacts and reveals he knows exactly who Silas is—he hired her because of Kernvall, wanting her guilt as leverage. He demands she help him quietly strip the cave before authorities learn of it, or he exposes her. POV: Silas, with a tense dialogue-driven scene. Emotional beat: betrayal compounding betrayal.

chapters.title: Fault Lines
chapters.summary: Tomas catches Silas copying Wren's journal pages by lamplight. Instead of blackmail, he confesses his testimony was coerced by the same insurers who blacklisted her. An uneasy alliance forms; the crew begins to fracture over Vane's escalating demands. POV shifts between Silas and Tomas. Emotional beat: loyalty rebuilt from shared damage.

chapters.title: The Glacier Answers
chapters.summary: Second and final tide window. As they enter, the glacier groans—calving early. Icefall blocks the exit route mid-expedition; Vane orders the artifacts carried out regardless, endangering everyone. Silas refuses, and the crew must choose. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: fear transmuted into command.

chapters.title: Six Hours to Dawn
chapters.summary: Climax. Silas leads the team through collapsing ice tunnels using the cave's ancient markers—which turn out to be navigation aids left by survivors like Wren. They find Wren alive, half-feral, guarding the site. Vane, fleeing alone with stolen relics, is caught by the calving shelf. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: sacrifice, reunion, reckoning.

chapters.title: Where the Compass Rests
chapters.summary: Resolution. Silas tells the rescue authorities everything—the truth about Kernvall, the coerced testimony, all of it. Her name is cleared enough to guide again, though not to be invisible. Wren, recovering, asks why she came back; Silas answers that staying was the first brave thing she'd ever done. POV: Silas. Emotional beat: belonging chosen, not stumbled into.
